coverage.note: The local total sums only published counts. Null counts are excluded, not treated as zero. Use this local sum for area share calculations; Table 2.1 is a separate national series with different coverage.

notes: Counts and confidence bounds are converted from thousands to individuals. Income remains in pounds. Published rounding is retained.

All source authority codes are retained, including Sheffield E08000019 and Barnsley E08000016. Home Office asylum tables use E08000039 and E08000038 respectively; consumers must apply their existing code resolver, not duplicate these rows.

Torbay E06000027 and Isles of Scilly E06000053 have source rows in both tables. Missing values are marked [Not available] by HMRC, not caused by a failed code join. Row notes identify the unavailable fields. No reason for individual cell suppression is inferred.
These are income taxpayers, not all residents or workers. Subnational estimates require caution; see the source notes. No local confidence bounds are summed to invent a national confidence interval.

sourceNotes.text: Estimates for sub-UK geographical areas (eg by country, region, county etc) should be treated with particular caution (please refer to the supporting documentation section 'Precision of estimates: sub UK areas').

Tables 3.13 to 3.15a do not include individuals added to the SPI through the supplementary PAYE sample introduced in the 2023 to 2024 tax year. As a result, these tables do not fully capture individuals whose sole source of income is the state pension, nor those who receive a state pension alongside small amounts of savings income that did not require submission of a Self Assessment return. Totals in these tables may not align with those presented in earlier SPI tables. For more information, please refer to the supporting documentation.

Individuals are allocated to regions and countries according to the residence of the recipient. The postcode has been used to determine the county and hence the region for the overwhelming majority of cases. Some members of the Forces and Merchant Navy, together with a small number of people serving overseas and people with overseas addresses have not been allocated to regions, but have been included in the UK figures. There are also a small number of people in the sample where it was not possible to identify their postcode and therefore identify the correct region. These have also been included in the UK figures. This explains why the regional amounts do not add up to the UK total.

projectionAssumptions.text: Projected estimates based upon the 2023 to 2024 Survey of Personal Incomes using economic assumptions consistent with the OBR’s March 2026 Economic and Fiscal Outlook.
